newsitem.title: USA: GAO says US bank regulators should be consolidated.
newsitem.headline: GAO says US bank regulators should be consolidated.

text.p: The General Accounting Office Wednesday recommended that the number of federal agencies responsible for banking oversight be reduced.

The congressional watchdog agency, after examining bank regulatory systems in five countries, said that if Congress decides to modernise the existing U.S. system, consolidation of regulatory responsibilities would be a logical step.

Specifically, it said that the Office of Thrift Supervision (OTS), which oversees national savings and loans, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), which supervises national banks, and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. (FDIC), which regulates federally insured, state chartered banks that are not Federal Reserve members, could be combined.

"This new independent agency, together with the Federal Reserve, could be assigned responsibility for consolidated, comprehensive supervision of these banking organisations under its purview," the GAO report said.
It said the the U.S. central bank should have direct access to supervisory information as well as influence over supervisory decision-making and the banking industry.

The GAO said this could be accomplished in a number of ways, including having the Fed keep its current oversight reponsibilities, or, alternatively, having it represented on the board of the new combined agency.

The Fed, in agency comments in the report, said it felt that the GAO shoud be specific in stating that the central bank needs "active supervisory involvement in the largest U.S. banking organisations and a cross-section of other banking institutions" to carry out its key central bank functions.
